problems.title: Keep a radical graph in quadrantI
problems.question: Which listed a makes y=√(x+a)+4a+5 lie only in quadrant I?
problems.idea: Use exact identities and geometric ratios, and check the domain and consistency of the data.
formulas: The domain begins at x=−a and the minimum y is 4a+5.
steps: For a=−1, the domain is x≥1 and y≥1, entirely in quadrant I. More generally, strictly positive coordinates require−5/4<a<0. Only −1 is listed.

problems.title: Extract even powers with absolute values
problems.question: Simplify√(−a⁵b⁷c⁸).
problems.idea: Use exact identities and geometric ratios, and check the domain and consistency of the data.
formulas: Factor the radicand as a⁴b⁶c⁸(−ab). Square roots of squared factors give a²|b³|c⁴.
steps: On the domain ab≤0, the result is a²|b³|c⁴√(−ab).
problems.note: If c=0, the original expression is 0 even when ab>0; that zero case must be handled separately because the simplified radical√(−ab) would otherwise be undefined.

problems.title: Inverse on the increasing parabola branch
problems.question: Find the inverse of y=x²−4x+5 for x≥2.
problems.idea: Use exact identities and geometric ratios, and check the domain and consistency of the data.
steps: Interchange variables to get y=2+√(x−1), with inverse domain x≥1.

problems.title: Perpendicular diagonals from a right half-triangle
problems.question: A parallelogram has diagonals6,8 and one side 5. Find are a.
problems.idea: Use exact identities and geometric ratios, and check the domain and consistency of the data.
formulas: The diagonals bisect each other. The half-diagonal triangle has sides 3,4,5, so the diagonals are perpendicular.

problems.title: Isosceles trapezoid area
problems.question: An isosceles trapezoid has bases2,8 and legs5. Find are a.
problems.idea: Use exact identities and geometric ratios, and check the domain and consistency of the data.
formulas: The horizontal side offset is(8−2)/2=3. Height=√(25−9)=4.

problems.title: Equal integer parts
problems.question: If floor(x)=floor(y), which listed conclusion must hold?
problems.idea: Use exact identities and geometric ratios, and check the domain and consistency of the data.
formulas: For some integer k, both x, y lie in[k, k+1).
steps: Their difference has absolute value strictly less than 1. Equality of the numbers or their magnitudes is not forced.

problems.title: Rationalize a conjugate
problems.question: Simplify2/(√7−√5)−√7.
problems.idea: Use exact identities and geometric ratios, and check the domain and consistency of the data.
formulas: The fraction equals 2(√7+√5)/(7−5)=√7+√5.
steps: Subtracting√7 leaves√5.

problems.title: Intersections of a fourth power and a square-root shift
problems.question: How many intersections have y=x⁴ and y=√x+1?
problems.idea: Use exact identities and geometric ratios, and check the domain and consistency of the data.
formulas: The shared domain is x≥0. For0≤x≤1, x⁴≤1<√x+1, so no equality occurs.
steps: For x≥1, the equation is √x(x^(7/2)−1)=1. Its left side is continuous and strictly increasing from 0 to∞, so it equals 1 exactly once.

problems.title: A small diagonal triangle determines a trapezoid
problems.question: Trapezoid BC∥AD has BC=1, AD=5, and are a BOC=4 at the diagonal intersection. Find whole are a.
problems.idea: Use exact identities and geometric ratios, and check the domain and consistency of the data.
formulas: The small triangle height is 2·4/1=8. The diagonal intersection splits the height in ratio1:5, so total height=6·8=48.
steps: Trapezoid are a=(1+5)·48/2=144.

problems.title: Medians with inconsistent angles and lengths
problems.question: Medians from A, C make17°,13° with AC, and have lengths 6,12. Find triangle are a.
problems.idea: Use exact identities and geometric ratios, and check the domain and consistency of the data.
formulas: If G is the centroid, GA=4 and GC=8. But triangle AGC has angles17°,13°,150°, so the sine rule requires GA/GC=sin13°/sin17°≈0.769, not1/2.
steps: Thus no triangle satisfies every stated datum. Ignoring this inconsistency, the formal are a calculation is are a ABC=3·(1/2)·4·8sin150°=24.
problems.answer: The full data are inconsistent; the formal listed calculation is 24.
problems.note: Even swapping the two median lengths gives ratio2, which still does not equal sin13°/sin17°. The individual angles and length ratio cannot coexist.

problems.title: An absolute-value inequality
problems.question: Solve|3x−1|≤|−5|.
problems.idea: Use exact identities and geometric ratios, and check the domain and consistency of the data.
steps: Add1 and divide by 3 to get−4/3≤x≤2.

problems.title: One intersection on each side of a pole
problems.question: Count intersections of y=x³−1 and y=1/x+2.
problems.idea: Use exact identities and geometric ratios, and check the domain and consistency of the data.
formulas: The equation is h(x)=x³−3−1/x=0, x≠0. Its derivative is 3x²+1/x²>0 on each branch.
steps: On(−∞,0), h increases from −∞ to∞; on(0,∞), it also increases from −∞ to∞. Each branch therefore contributes one root.

problems.title: An increasing rational function on a closed interval
problems.question: Which listed a makes(3x−17)/(x+a) increasing on[−8,4]?
problems.idea: Use exact identities and geometric ratios, and check the domain and consistency of the data.
formulas: The derivative is(3a+17)/(x+a)². Strict increase requires3a+17>0, and the pole−a must stay outside the interval.
steps: For a=−5, the numerator2>0 and pole5 lies beyond4. Other listed a-values either give a negative derivative or place a pole inside the interval.

problems.title: Parallelogram area from two altitudes
problems.question: Altitudes from an acute parallelogram vertex are 4,6 and form150°. Find its are a.
problems.idea: Use exact identities and geometric ratios, and check the domain and consistency of the data.
formulas: The original acute angle is 30°. If the sides are a, b, the altitudes are bsin30°, asin30°.
steps: Area=ab sin30°=(4·6)/sin30°=48.

problems.title: A point on a median from two areas
problems.question: M lies on median AD. Areas ABM=8, DCM=6. Find AM:AD.
problems.idea: Use exact identities and geometric ratios, and check the domain and consistency of the data.
formulas: Because BD=DC, areas DBM and DCM are equal, so DBM=6. Triangles ABM and DBM share the altitude from B to AD.
steps: Thus AM:MD=8:6=4:3, so AM:AD=4:7.

problems.title: Equal fractional parts as a locus
problems.question: What is the set of points satisfying{x}={y}?
problems.idea: Use exact identities and geometric ratios, and check the domain and consistency of the data.
formulas: Write x=floor(x)+{x}, y=floor(y)+{y}. Equal fractional parts mean x−y is an integer.
steps: Conversely an integer difference preserves the fractional part. Thus the locus is the family y=x+k, k integer.

problems.title: A cube-root quotient
problems.question: Evaluate(∛4−⁶√4)/(∛(2⁵)−∛16).
problems.idea: Use exact identities and geometric ratios, and check the domain and consistency of the data.
formulas: Put t=∛2. Then the numerator is t²−t and denominator2t²−2t.
steps: Since t≠1, the common factor cancels, giving1/2.

problems.title: A difference of cubes inside a quotient
problems.question: Simplify(b√b+a√(−a))/(√b−√(−a)).
problems.idea: Use exact identities and geometric ratios, and check the domain and consistency of the data.
formulas: Put u=√b, v=√(−a). The numerator is u³−v³, and denominator u−v.
steps: The quotient is u²+uv+v²=b−a+√(−ab).
problems.note: Require b≥0, a≤0 and b≠−a so the original denominator is nonzero.

problems.title: Heights at least as long as their bases
problems.question: Every parallelogram altitude is at least its corresponding base. Find the angle between diagonals.
problems.idea: Use exact identities and geometric ratios, and check the domain and consistency of the data.
formulas: For side lengths a, b and angleθ, the conditions are bsinθ≥a and asinθ≥b.
steps: Multiplying gives sin²θ≥1, so θ=90°. The inequalities then force a=b. The parallelogram is a square, whose diagonals are perpendicular.

problems.title: Bisectors in two isosceles half-triangles
problems.question: ABC is right at B, M midpoint AC. Angle bisectors MD, ME in ABM, BMC meet AB, BC; DE meets BM at K. If are a DBK=8, find are a ABC.
problems.idea: Use exact identities and geometric ratios, and check the domain and consistency of the data.
formulas: MA=MB=MC, so those bisectors also bisect bases AB, BC. Thus D, E are side midpoints, and K is midpoint BM.
steps: Use B=(0,0), A=(a,0), C=(0, c). Then D=(a/2,0), K=(a/4, c/4), so are a DBK=ac/16.
Area ABC=ac/2 is 8 times as large, hence64.

problems.title: Coefficient sums by evaluation at1
problems.question: Two radical sums f₁, f₂ have rational coefficients whose respective sums are 1. Find the coefficient sum of their product.
problems.idea: Use exact identities and geometric ratios, and check the domain and consistency of the data.
formulas: At x=1, every radical power equals 1. Therefore f₁(1)=f₂(1)=1.
steps: The sum of coefficients of the expanded product equals its value at 1, which is 1·1=1.

problems.title: A symmetric pair of equations
problems.question: Given y=√(x+1), y=x²−1 and x>0, which listed relation follows?
problems.idea: Use exact identities and geometric ratios, and check the domain and consistency of the data.
formulas: Both x, y are positive. Squaring gives y²=x+1, and the second gives x²=y+1.
steps: Subtract:(x−y)(x+y)=−(x−y), or(x−y)(x+y+1)=0. The second factor is positive, so x=y.

problems.title: An absolute-value quartic
problems.question: Find the product of real roots of|2x²+1−x⁴|+|x⁴−2x²+2|=7.
problems.idea: Use exact identities and geometric ratios, and check the domain and consistency of the data.
formulas: Put t=x⁴−2x²=(x²−1)²−1≥−1. The equation becomes|1−t|+t+2=7.
steps: For t≤1, the left side is 3, so no roots. For t>1, it gives 2t+1=7, t=3.
Then x⁴−2x²−3=(x²−3)(x²+1)=0. The real roots are±√3, product −3.

problems.title: A45° bisector fixes an area ratio
problems.question: A right trapezoid has height AB equal to its base sum BC+AD. The bisector of∠ABC meets extended AD at N. Find are a ABCD:are a ABN.
problems.idea: Use exact identities and geometric ratios, and check the domain and consistency of the data.
formulas: ∠ABC=90°, so the bisector gives an isosceles right triangle ABN with AN=AB=h.
steps: Triangle are a=h²/2. Trapezoid are a=(BC+AD)h/2=h²/2 as well.

problems.title: Area equality forces a parallelogram
problems.question: Diagonals meet at K in convex ABCD. Areas ABK=DCK=1, total are a≤4, and AD=6. Find BC.
problems.idea: Use exact identities and geometric ratios, and check the domain and consistency of the data.
formulas: Opposite diagonal-triangle are a products agree, so if BCK=t, then DAK=1/t. Total are a=2+t+1/t≥4.
steps: The upper bound forces equality:t=1. All 4 small areas equal 1, so both diagonals bisect each other.
Thus ABCD is a parallelogram and BC=AD=6.
